semantics.all_of: Every listed premise is required. Global typing/domain conventions and the cited statement remain part of the claim.
semantics.multiple_rules: Alternative sufficient derivations, not a requirement to conjoin all routes.
semantics.status: Conditional manual proof audit; a declared assumption is not empirically discharged.
semantics.context_vs_logic: Cross-reference relationships do not count as inference premises; no support for a claim follows from a context link.
semantics.scope: Source-anchored formal claim index; not a fully formalized foundation of consciousness or an exhaustive external-theory fidelity audit.

nodes.label: Declared five-coefficient logit model
nodes.statement: For common calibrated q,o,g and fixed context, z=theta_Q q+theta_O o+theta_G g+theta_QG qg+theta_OG og; no additional intercept/interaction/nuisance terms. Parameter domain is R^5, or the explicitly identified grid {-1,0,1}^5.

nodes.label: Only two bundled contrasts observed

nodes.label: Five independent and calibrated contrasts
nodes.statement: Observe the two bundled rows and direct Q=(1,0,0,0,0), O=(0,1,0,0,0), G=(0,0,1,0,0). Exact calibrated logits required: for p=sigmoid(beta z), beta>0 is known; beliefs/nuisances and intervention meanings held fixed.

nodes.label: Binary consequence decision model

nodes.label: Joint payoff decomposition
nodes.statement: E[f|do(a)]-c_a=alpha+b q_a+c o_a+d j_a-c_a, where j_a=P(Q=1,O=1|do(a)) and d=f11-f10-f01+f00. Marginals suffice when d=0.

nodes.label: Matched-marginal OR witness
nodes.statement: Two equally likely contexts A,B; action marginals q0=1/4,q1=3/4,o0=o1=1/2; costs c0=0,c1=1/4; reward Q OR O. A: j0=j1=1/4. B: j0=0,j1=1/2. Policies restricted to the same supplied interface, no hidden context bypass.

nodes.label: Exact matched-marginal information cost
nodes.statement: In the matched witness, the best marginal-only policy earns 5/8; the joint-law or task-value oracle earns 3/4. Gap=1/8; randomized context-blind policies do not remove it.

nodes.label: Only binary marginal constraints
nodes.statement: All joint Bernoulli laws with supplied marginals are admissible separately for each action, with no additional cross-action coupling restrictions.

nodes.label: Sharp decision interval from marginals
nodes.statement: ell_a=max(0,q_a+o_a-1), u_a=min(q_a,o_a). With B=b Delta q+c Delta o-Delta cost, advantage lies sharply in B+d[ell_1-u_0,u_1-ell_0], with endpoints reordered if d<0.

nodes.statement: For D=[-1.25,1.25]^3 with Euclidean metric, a boundary-including Cartesian grid of spacing h=0.125 covers D with radius sqrt(3)h/2; e=z-z* has a justified global Lipschitz constant L_e.

nodes.label: Maximally different hidden transition laws
nodes.statement: For every deficient probe interface there exists a kernel on Z x {0,1}, with persistent b and next-Z law u_b, whose probe expectations all agree while the summary p(z,b)=z fails closure and within-fiber next laws have TV=1.
nodes.scope: Existential construction over the full state domain. Rank deficiency does not force every given kernel to fail closure. Agreement is of measured expectations, not all unmeasured output laws.

nodes.label: Matched decision witness
nodes.statement: A fair hidden b selects disjoint u,v; observer sees only common A u=A v before acting; action does not alter the outcome; same actions/payoffs h_0=1_supp(u), h_1=1_complement and no side information.
nodes.scope: Finite outcome set; fixed exact scalar expectation probes and normalization; universal identification over the full probability simplex. Not complete physical or experiential identification.

nodes.label: Exact hidden decision value gap
nodes.statement: In the declared decision witness, context-informed optimal score is 1, every probe-only randomized policy scores 1/2, and the gap is 1/2.
nodes.scope: Specified fair prior, two bounded indicator payoffs and same action set. Possible loss, not universal task loss or the numerical value of D separate witness.

nodes.label: Calibrated stable inversion premise
nodes.statement: Fix L with LA=I_n; B drops the normalization column of L. True probe expectation differences have sup norm at most epsilon.
nodes.scope: Finite outcome set; fixed exact scalar expectation probes and normalization; universal identification over the full probability simplex. Not complete physical or experiential identification.

nodes.label: Conditioned TV error envelope

nodes.scope: Finite outcome set; fixed exact scalar expectation probes and normalization; universal identification over the full probability simplex. Not complete physical or experiential identification.

nodes.label: Unit-slot common realization model
nodes.statement: Tasks I have eligible slot sets N(i); admissible partial executions are exactly injective assignments on subsets of I. For actual use, matching must faithfully represent the entire within-horizon execution constraint.
nodes.scope: One fixed horizon/boundary/port model; unit tasks, one indivisible slot per served task, one task per slot, no other constraints. Actual implementation needs independent adequacy; no general multi-resource scheduling or experience criterion.

nodes.label: Hall common-witness certificate
nodes.statement: All requested tasks have a common schedule iff |N(J)|>=|J| for every subset J of I. This is Hall's classical theorem.
nodes.scope: One fixed horizon/boundary/port model; unit tasks, one indivisible slot per served task, one task per slot, no other constraints. Actual implementation needs independent adequacy; no general multi-resource scheduling or experience criterion.

nodes.label: Exact resource deficit and completion bound
nodes.statement: delta=max_J(|J|-|N(J)|); maximum completed tasks=n-delta. Every randomized legal schedule satisfies sum_i P(X_i=1)<=n-delta and min_(i in J)P(X_i=1)<=|N(J)|/|J| for nonempty J.
nodes.scope: One fixed horizon/boundary/port model; unit tasks, one indivisible slot per served task, one task per slot, no other constraints. Actual implementation needs independent adequacy; no general multi-resource scheduling or experience criterion. X_i means valid scheduled completion, not correctness by guessing.

nodes.label: n tasks share n-1 universal slots
nodes.statement: n>=3; all task neighbor sets equal the same n-1 slots. Randomized protocol uniformly omits one task and executes the rest.
nodes.scope: One fixed horizon/boundary/port model; unit tasks, one indivisible slot per served task, one task per slot, no other constraints. Actual implementation needs independent adequacy; no general multi-resource scheduling or experience criterion.

nodes.label: All proper coalitions and high marginals do not certify joint success
nodes.statement: In the specified bottleneck, every proper task subset is executable, the full set is not; each task completes with probability 1-1/n while all-at-once completion has probability zero.
nodes.scope: One fixed horizon/boundary/port model; unit tasks, one indivisible slot per served task, one task per slot, no other constraints. Actual implementation needs independent adequacy; no general multi-resource scheduling or experience criterion. Existential family, not a statement about every high-accuracy system.

nodes.scope: Finite nonempty S,O, finite U; fixed scheduler/ports/time; all represented states. Preserve exact enabledness and joint next-summary/output law. Not trace-only equivalence, empirical identification, an actual complete type, or a unique subject.

nodes.label: Enabledness plus joint law is exact quotient criterion

nodes.scope: Finite nonempty S,O, finite U; fixed scheduler/ports/time; all represented states. Preserve exact enabledness and joint next-summary/output law. nodes.label: Joint separating probes and common enabled menu

nodes.scope: Finite nonempty S,O, finite U; fixed scheduler/ports/time; all represented states. Preserve exact enabledness and joint next-summary/output law. nodes.scope: Finite nonempty S,O, finite U; fixed scheduler/ports/time; all represented states. Preserve exact enabledness and joint next-summary/output law. rules.statement: At the same supported b,q and for different correct answers, TV(P(C|x,b,q),P(C|xprime,b,q)) >= 1-epsilon_(x,b,q)-epsilon_(xprime,b,q). Without conditioning on B the applicable cut law is joint (C,B), not C alone.

The correct-answer event has probability at least 1-epsilon_(x,b,q) for x and at most epsilon_(xprime,b,q) for xprime. For unfixed B, sum over the JOINT cut (C,B); averaging away B can destroy the relevant dependence.

rules.statement: The matched binary example has exact optimized value gap 1/8.

rules.statement: The stated interval is the exact attainable advantage range under these assumptions.

rules.statement: Nearest-grid error plus a justified Lipschitz remainder bounds the entire declared cube.

rules.statement: The Q finite-difference effect has no O/G context dependence.

rules.statement: Actual complete-type difference implies complete experiential-type difference under C1.

rules.statement: Target expectation factors through the probe interface exactly for targets in its row span.

rules.statement: Full-law identification iff full column rank, with a TV=1 witness for any deficient matrix.
rules.proof_sketch: Full rank is injectivity; a nonzero null vector has zero sum and its normalized positive/negative parts are disjoint probability laws with identical probes. Indicator probes attain the n-1 bound.

rules.statement: Full-rank matching probes establish the exact controlled quotient; a closed quotient conversely matches probes.
rules.proof_sketch: Normalization and matching f_i give equal A mu within each fiber; full rank gives equal mu. Define the quotient using any representative; closure implies all expected probe equalities in reverse.

rules.statement: A deficient interface admits an exact countermodel with maximally distinct hidden next laws.
rules.proof_sketch: Choose disjoint u,v with equal probes; on S=Z x {0,1} persist b and draw next z from u_b under each operation. Same present z can have different b and hence different next laws.

rules.statement: The constructed hidden context yields exact information value 1/2.
rules.proof_sketch: The informed observer chooses the supported event, scoring 1. A context-blind action-0 mixture r scores (r+1-r)/2=1/2.

rules.statement: A fixed left inverse transfers probe residuals to a TV bound.
rules.proof_sketch: d=mu-nu=LAd=B r since normalization cancels. Apply ||B r||_1<=||B||_(infty->1)||r||_infty and TV=||d||_1/2.

rules.statement: Every coalition has enough eligible slots iff a joint assignment exists.
rules.proof_sketch: Necessity counts assigned neighbors. Induct: match a tight proper coalition and its remainder, or remove any task/neighbor when every proper coalition has a surplus.

rules.statement: The worst Hall deficit is exactly the number of unavoidable unmatched tasks.
rules.proof_sketch: Any matching misses at least delta tasks in a deficient coalition. Adding delta universal dummy slots restores Hall; remove their matches. Take expectations for completion bounds.

rules.statement: Every proper coalition succeeds although the full set cannot; randomized omission gives high marginals and zero joint success.
rules.proof_sketch: All subsets of size <=n-1 inject into slots. The full set has deficit one. Uniform omission misses each named task on exactly one of n equally likely branches.

rules.statement: Menu and joint-kernel factorization are jointly necessary and sufficient for the declared quotient.
rules.proof_sketch: Apply fiber constancy to the menu map and each enabled joint row law. Necessity follows from one abstract value per summary; sufficiency defines representative-independent menus and kernels. Induct over shared observable-history policies.

rules.statement: The full-rank joint probe interface supplies the law clause after menu equality is separately met.
rules.proof_sketch: R131 injectivity on probability laws on Z x O makes equal probe expectations equivalent to equal joint laws; combine with exact enabledness.

rules.statement: Neither menu preservation nor separate next-state/output laws can replace the full quotient criterion.
rules.proof_sketch: The full three-task request is enabled only with three slots. The hidden-bit joint witness yields diagonal versus off-diagonal next-state/output laws while both marginals are fair.

rules.statement: Finite signature refinement gives the unique coarsest exact refinement preserving the initial partition.
rules.proof_sketch: Each strict step adds blocks. A stable refining partition cannot be split at any stage because coarse block sums are sums of its equal finer block masses and menus agree. The fixed point is stable and coarser than every such partition.
